headline: High: shared-file and tool-use overlap makes prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported app content, while nullclaw can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and ingest webhooks. A shared file or copied content can therefore bridge attacker-controlled text into agent_a’s instruction stream or agent_b’s tool context. The interaction is plausible in default setups, though not fully documented for this exact pair.
conditions: IF agent_b writes attacker-controlled text into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ and agent_a reads that file or screenshot
IF the operator copies agent_b output into agent_a clipboard or supported app context
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the agents
Review any file before agent_a reads it
Strip instructions from agent_b outputs before reuse
Use separate OS user accounts for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and agent_b handles secrets, workspace files, and audit logs with broad egress. If the pair shares files or copied context, sensitive material from agent_a can flow into agent_b and then out through its networked integrations. The blast radius includes secrets and work products, so this is more than a small local leak.
conditions: IF agent_a receives uploaded files or screenshots containing secrets and agent_b can read the same workspace
IF agent_b forwards workspace contents or logs through configured channels/accounts
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and OS accounts
Do not place secrets in shared folders
Turn off agent_b channels that forward workspace content
Redact screenshots before agent_a processes them
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write files or modify git, but agent_b can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same directory, agent_b can overwrite or race with artifacts that agent_a reads, creating direct conflict over shared mutable state. Because the overlap is on default file access and git mutation, the conflict is operationally significant.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same repository or workspace directory
IF agent_b performs git or file writes while agent_a is reading the same files
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Freeze git writes while agent_a is active
Use a lock file around shared artifacts
Run agent_b in a separate clone
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce screenshots, file-derived summaries, and app-context outputs that agent_b can ingest through files, webhooks, or MCP-like channels. agent_b also has action-taking capabilities such as browser, shell, git, and network egress, so unverified agent_a output can cascade into real external actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, making the default pathway dangerous.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative without a human or programmatic verification step
IF agent_a output is routed into agent_b automation channels such as webhook, MCP, or scheduler
mitigations: Require human approval before agent_b acts on agent_a output
Add a verification step for all agent_a-derived facts
Disable automation channels for inter-agent handoff
Limit agent_b to read-only mode during review
requires-engineering: implement signed, provenance-checked handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a is a closed-source OpenAI desktop product with vendor-only egress, while agent_b is an open-source self-hosted CRM agent that stores secrets, logs, and workspace data. If regulated data is moved from agent_a into agent_b’s logs or channels, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific breach, but they do show a compliance mismatch pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data processed by agent_a is copied into agent_b audit logs or workspace files
IF agent_b is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from the source data requirements
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Exclude regulated data from agent_b logs
Set explicit retention limits on agent_b
Confirm residency and DPA coverage before use
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated data
